title: Annotatio III §.VII (3) close: Defense of the charitable colloquy; Rinteln Epistola Apologetica; Maresius/Hornbeck/Heidegger — stop before §.VIII
pass_a_gloss: (3.) That either party of the Colloquents diligently and learnedly defended their Charitable colloquy against detractors and whatever haters of Protestant Peace, and earned the fullest applause of almost all foreign Protestants; that even the Rinteln Apologetic Letter — owed to a pair of Theologians of sublime Judgment and manifold Erudition, Peter Musaeus and John Hennichius as Authors — was translated into other languages. Compare the Defense of the Cassel Colloquy of Maresius, Hornbeck, Heidegger, etc.
pass_b_english: (3.) Both colloquy sides vigorously and learnedly defended their charitable colloquy against detractors and every hater of Protestant peace, and won near-universal applause from foreign Protestants.
Even the Rinteln Epistola Apologetica — by that pair of high-judgment, many-sided theologians Peter Musaeus and John Hennichius — was translated into other languages.
Compare the Cassel Colloquy defenses of Maresius, Hornbeck, Heidegger, and others.
Stop before §. VIII (fruits of Lipsiacum and Cassellanum into the present age).
source_text: (3.) Quòd utraque Colloquentium pars colloquium suum Charitativum contra obtrectatores Pacisque Protestanticae osores quoscunque, impigre doctéque defenderit, & exterorum Protestantium propemodum omnium amplissimum applausum meruerit; Rintelensium etiam Epistola Apologetica, sublimis Judicii ac multijugae Eruditionis Theologorum biga, Petro Museo & Joh. Hennichio Auctoribus debita, in alias linguas translata sit. Confer Defension. Colloq. Cassel. Maresii, Hornbeckii, Heideggeri &c.
notes: Cassellanum mark (3) close; natural stop before §.VIII fruits.
